text: A path has an 80 ms round-trip time and 1% packet loss. A single TCP stream achieves about 15 Mb/s on a 1 Gb/s circuit that is 25% utilised. What is the binding constraint?
choices: Packet loss, which caps single-stream TCP throughput by the inverse square root of the loss rate
The circuit is oversubscribed at peak
A duplex mismatch on the far end
explanation: The Mathis relation gives throughput proportional to (MSS/RTT) x 1/sqrt(p). At 1% loss with a 1,460-byte MSS and 80 ms RTT, the ceiling is around 15 Mb/s regardless of link capacity. Upgrading the circuit changes nothing; finding the source of the loss does.
